label: ext.blocktype ext.blocktype
createStatement: CREATE (b:ext.blocktype {id: $id, name: $name, properties: $properties, requiredProperties: $requiredProperties, semantics: $semantics, status: $status})

createParameters.name: ext.blocktype

properties.block: true marks the type a block: addressable, ordered, containable through CONTAINS
properties.name: the domain node type the Block describes; unique among established definitions, so the definition set is an unambiguous namespace
properties.optionalProperties: content properties the described type may carry and need not; declaring one is what makes it enforceable, since an undeclared property stays tolerated
properties.permittedChildTypes: block types this type may contain; empty on a leaf
properties.permittedValues: map of property name to the values that property may hold; applies to required and optional properties alike, and a property absent from the map is unconstrained in value. Narrowing a set is a breaking definition change, widening is not
properties.requiredProperties: content properties the described type requires
properties.runProperties: content properties holding formatted text as runs
properties.singleOpenCandidate: true keeps at most one open candidate revision per node
properties.uniqueProperties: content properties unique among established revisions of the type

createParameters.semantics: Describes a domain node type an extension defines. Validation enforces established definitions: content claiming the type is checked for required properties and the block-vocabulary declarations, a definition never shadows a code-registered type, and a breaking definition change requires an ext.migration Block in its proposal group. The meta-schema's own definition Blocks are ext.blocktype Blocks, so the conventions describe themselves.
